misconceptions.description: Phrasing the study question around appeal or engagement instead of a design feature and an observable learner outcome
misconceptions.trigger: learner asks whether the storyboard is engaging, appealing, or finished rather than what specific frame change moves a measurable behavior
misconceptions.feedback: Name the design feature you changed and the learner action you can observe. Engagement is not the variable a small study can interpret.

misconceptions.description: Stating a desired outcome without tying it to the specific storyboard element believed to cause it
misconceptions.trigger: learner names a goal (better learning, less confusion) but no signaling cue, frame, or narration choice that the study would manipulate
misconceptions.feedback: Connect the outcome to one concrete design element (a signaling cue, a frame order, a reader-action prompt) so the question points at something you can change.

misconceptions.description: Writing a question so broad that no observation could confirm or disconfirm it
misconceptions.trigger: question uses vague terms like improve learning with no comparison, measure, or bounded design change
misconceptions.feedback: Bind the question to one design change and one observable action so a result could come out either way.
